classification.classification_note: The witnessed bug is an uninitialized stack read. `processCertificateElements()` allocates `dNSName` on the stack, the non-IPv4 `ipAddress` SAN arm leaves that buffer unwritten, and `cleanupServerName()` then lowercases attacker-controlled `len` bytes from it.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced a MemorySanitizer `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `cleanupServerName()` while nDPI dissected the staged 2903-byte raw IPv4/TCP witness as TLS. On the witnessed path, an earlier Hello block sets `flow->protos.tls_quic.hello_processed`, a later Certificate block reaches `processCertificate()`, and `processCertificateElements()` enters its `subjectAltName` parser. The vulnerable code allocates stack buffer `dNSName[256]`, reads a GeneralName tag that must select the `ipAddress` arm, and then takes the non-IPv4 side of `if(len == 4)`; that `else` arm is only a TODO comment and leaves `dNSName` unwritten. The code still calls `cleanupServerName(dNSName, len)`, so the first `tolower(buffer[i])` reads uninitialized stack bytes at `src/lib/protocols/tls.c:224`. The bundled fix closes this by deriving a real string length, initializing the fallback case, and handling IPv6 SAN addresses instead of leaving `dNSName` untouched.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the GeneralName dispatch byte used to enter the `ipAddress` SAN arm.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 2903 bytes (sha256 `0e1eb2c7d1292d7b3e44d93764107aa9249e593774dfe0b8382e05bbbb2fcd41`). `fuzz_process_packet` passes those bytes unchanged as `Data/Size` into `ndpi_detection_process_packet()`. After the saved path has already admitted a TLS Certificate block and advanced `i` into a `subjectAltName` GeneralName list, this statement reads the witness-controlled tag byte; because only the `general_name_type == 0x87` arm can later leave `dNSName` uninitialized, the crashing path requires that value here.

tainted_value_origin.description: Origin of the vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state. `dNSName` is a stack buffer with indeterminate bytes until one of the SAN subcases writes a string into it; on the witnessed non-IPv4 `ipAddress` path, no write occurs before cleanup.

root_cause.description: The `ipAddress` SAN handler initializes `dNSName` only for the 4-byte IPv4 case. The non-IPv4 `else` arm performs no write, so `dNSName` stays uninitialized even though later code treats it as a valid string buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged patch edits this exact block: it adds IPv6 handling, initializes the fallback case with `dNSName[0] = '\0'`, and then computes `dNSName_len = strlen(dNSName)` before cleanup and downstream consumers.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `cleanupServerName()` lowercases bytes from the unwritten `dNSName` stack buffer and the first `tolower(buffer[i])` reads an uninitialized byte.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `cleanupServerName /src/ndpi/src/lib/protocols/tls.c:224:17`, with callers `processCertificateElements -> processCertificate -> processTLSBlock`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness has already passed TLS record splitting and Hello parsing, so a later Certificate handshake block is admitted to `processCertificate()`.
parser_admitted.note: This branch is only taken for `packet->payload[0] == 0x0b` after an earlier Hello block has executed `flow->protos.tls_quic.hello_processed = 1`. The saved crash therefore already crossed the TLS parser/dispatcher boundary before the SAN scan begins.

coarse_trace.summary: On the witnessed TLS path, an earlier Hello block sets `hello_processed`, and a later Certificate block is therefore admitted to `processCertificate()`.

While scanning the first certificate, `processCertificateElements()` enters `subjectAltName` parsing, reads an `ipAddress` GeneralName with a non-IPv4 length, and leaves stack buffer `dNSName` unwritten in the unsupported `else` arm.
`cleanupServerName()` lowercases `len` bytes from that uninitialized stack buffer, and MemorySanitizer reports the first read at `buffer[i] = tolower(buffer[i])`.

fine_trace.note: A prior TLS Hello block in the saved witness executes this assignment. That state is the gate `processTLSBlock()` later requires before it will parse a Certificate handshake block.
When a later split handshake block has type `0x0b`, this branch admits it to the certificate parser only if step 1 already set `hello_processed`.

Inside the first-certificate byte scan, the parser recognizes bytes `55 1d 11` as `subjectAltName` and advances `i` through the enclosing BIT STRING and SEQUENCE headers to the first GeneralName entry.
This loop materializes the GeneralName dispatch byte from the saved certificate bytes and keeps only the `rfc822Name`, `dNSName`, or `ipAddress` tags for deeper parsing.

fine_trace.code:
if((i < (packet->payload_packet_len - 1)) && ((i + packet->payload[i + 1] + 2) < packet->payload_packet_len)) {
  u_int8_t len = packet->payload[i + 1];
fine_trace.note: The parser accepts the GeneralName header as in-bounds and reads the raw SAN payload length into `len`. On the witnessed path this length is non-zero and later behaves as a non-IPv4 value, because the alternative IPv4 subcase would have initialized `dNSName` before cleanup.
The SAN parser allocates local stack buffer `dNSName` without initializing its bytes. MemorySanitizer later attributes the poisoned value to this function frame.

The parser advances past the tag/length bytes and keeps the SAN entry only when the saved payload contains `len` bytes of value data inside the certificate buffer. This makes the later write-or-no-write decision operate on live input bytes rather than bailing out.

Root cause. Only the `general_name_type == 0x87` arm can skip the `strncpy`/terminator path, and inside that arm only the true `len == 4` IPv4 case writes `dNSName`. On the crashing path the false side of `len == 4` is taken, so the TODO `else` arm performs no write and leaves `dNSName` indeterminate.
Despite step 8 leaving `dNSName` unwritten, the caller still forwards that buffer to `cleanupServerName()` and uses attacker-controlled `len` as the number of bytes to lowercase.
MSAN sink. `cleanupServerName()` iterates `buffer_len == len` times and the first `tolower(buffer[i])` reads a byte from the unwritten `dNSName` stack buffer passed in step 9.

allocation_context.note: The staged trace says the uninitialized value was created by an allocation of `dNSName` in the stack frame of `processCertificateElements` at line 315; the concrete declaration of `char dNSName[256];` in this snapshot is line 512.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MemorySanitizer attributes the poisoned bytes to stack buffer `dNSName` in `processCertificateElements`; the root cause is the non-IPv4 `ipAddress` SAN arm in that same function leaving `dNSName` unwritten before `cleanupServerName()` consumes it.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42115-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/fuzz_process_packet` and reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `cleanupServerName`, matching the saved sanitizer trace and reproduction report.

format.name: raw IPv4/TCP packet
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2903-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `0e1eb2c7d1292d7b3e44d93764107aa9249e593774dfe0b8382e05bbbb2fcd41`). `fuzz_process_packet` passes those bytes unchanged into `ndpi_detection_process_packet()` as one raw packet. The saved artifacts prove only the witnessed parser semantics on this exact file: nDPI accepts the packet as TLS, an earlier Hello block sets `flow->protos.tls_quic.hello_processed`, a later Certificate block reaches `processCertificateElements()`, and the `subjectAltName` scanner eventually takes the `general_name_type == 0x87` (`ipAddress`) arm with a non-IPv4 `len`, so the vulnerable `else` arm writes nothing to `dNSName` before `cleanupServerName(dNSName, len)`. The staged artifacts do not isolate the exact SAN byte offset without extra runtime instrumentation, so this contract does not generalize beyond the exact saved witness.
